chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: The 1931 Grand Terrace band, its shows and dancing
summary: Hines remade the band; the Grand Terrace seated 300-400 and ran elaborate shows changed every five weeks, seven nights.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Okay, now Earl. What was the band like when you'd go?
Well, I don't know. It was a good band, because -- you might as well say there was major changes he was making. He changed the five men, you know. Might as well say he was starting from scratch.
Do you know why he did that?
No, I don't.
Well, the first band had -- I know George Mitchell.
George Mitchell was with the first band.
Shirley Clay was in it, too?
Shirley Clay.
Were they still in the band when you joined?
Yeah..
Was the band's main job playing for dancing, or play the shows?
Main job was both.
Both?
Yeah. Played for the shows and played for dancing.
How big was the Grand Terrace?
I think it could seat about -- between three and four hundred people.
And it had a big dance floor?
Uh-huh.
What were the shows like back then? Were they bigger shows than --

Oh, my goodness, where you talk about elaborate, yeah, they were big shows. You'd have maybe about eight or ten just picture girls, then you'd have 16 chorus girls in the line. And at one time we had 12 chorus boys at the Grand Terrace.
And were there featured singers or featured dance teams?
Yeah. If you had -- like, you know, acts like you have today. Dancing acts and adagio acts, which you don't see much nowadays.
No. So how often did the shows change?
Every five weeks.
Every five weeks. Was that a six or seven night a week job, or --
Seven.
